text:
maria: Heads-up — BlueHarbor security review in 24h. They asked specifically for the on‑prem keystore handoff and RBAC proof for tenant provisioning. Can we sketch what we can show without exposing key material?

dan: We can show role mappings + authz decision logs. No key material ever leaves HSM, we should call that out. Link to draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood/blueharbor-hand-off 

li: For logs, exporting a sampled audit stream is fine — include actions, actor, and resource. Use redaction for PII. Example: 
```
{"ts":"1737504000","actor":"svc-provision","action":"create_tenant","tenant":"blueharbor","role":"tenant_admin"}
```

oliver: BlueHarbor also asked for evidence of who can request a key unwrap. They want the approval flow recorded. Do we have an existing ticket workflow that ties to SSO+approval?

rachel: We do — requests go through JIRA change request, approval logged in our SSO. We can correlate JIRA ID -> SSO actor -> keystore audit event. Need to document retention windows. BlueHarbor requests 2y for audit logs.

maria: Is 2y allowed? We typically keep full audit for 1y then aggregated for 3y. Need legal check but product sec + infra can scope.

dan: Ops note: storing raw KMS audit for 2y increases retention cost. We can propose exported compressed JSON + indexes for forensic access. Also propose TTL-based redaction for tenant identifiers after N months.

li: On RBAC changes: if we show role mapping, add a small diagram + sample policy blob. E.g.: 
```json
{"role":"tenant_admin","permissions":["models:deploy","tenants:read","keys:request-unlock"]}
```

maria: BlueHarbor asked about emergency access / break-glass. We need to spell out the process and audit trail (time-limited tokens + escalation emails). Include sample incident play: breach simulation triggered, break-glass approved by two SAs, token auto-revoked after 30m.

oliver: They also asked for HSM attestation (FIPS level and module cert). We should attach certs in the packet and note whether the on‑prem deploy uses local HSM or cloud HSM. For their on‑prem pilot, it's local HSM.

rachel: Vulnerability triage note: they wanted how we handle a critical CVE in the crypto stack. Summary: notify customers within 24h of triage, apply staged patch on Dedicated, schedule forced upgrade for Private with rollback plan. Add CVE response template to the packet.

sec-bot: reminder: runbook template created for customer-hand-off v1.0 — https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/customer-hand-off-template

maria: Can someone pull a short export (redacted) showing a provisioning event + subsequent keystore access for demo tomorrow? Need it by EOD. 

dan: I’ll grab a 1-hour window and produce a redacted tarball: sample events, role mapping doc, and the JIRA->SSO correlation snippet. Expected file: blueharbor_handshake_redacted_2024-11-21.tgz

li: I’ll include the retention policy matrix and a small script to regenerate a redaction sample: 
```bash
# redacts tenant IDs
jq 'del(.tenant_id)' audit.json > audit.redacted.json
```

maria: Perfect. Oliver, can you confirm the call attendees on BlueHarbor side and whether they want a live demo or just artifacts?

oliver: Confirmed — they prefer artifacts + 15min Q&A. Attendees: infra lead, security architect, compliance mgr. I’ll send calendar invite.

maria: Great. Last ask — include a one‑page statement: "We never export key material. Access to unseal operations is logged and requires dual-approval for on‑prem deployments." Keep phrasing customer-facing.

rachel: Drafting that now, will drop into the packet and ping for review. :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks team. EOD deliverables: redacted export (dan), retention matrix (li), one-pager (rachel), certs + attestation (oliver). I’ll assemble and run through before the call.
